title: Tacrolimus and cyclosporine
effect: Tacrolimus: PRES, delirium, seizures and coma; also tremor, paresthesias, headache — linked to troughs at or above range (Prograf §5.6)
Cyclosporine: convulsions, especially with high-dose methylprednisolone; encephalopathy including PRES (Neoral Warnings)
pearls: Tacrolimus neurotoxicity: check the trough; consider dose reduction or stopping (Prograf §5.6)
Cyclosporine PRES risk factors: hypertension, hypomagnesemia, hypocholesterolemia, high-dose steroids, high cyclosporine levels, GVHD; liver > kidney transplant (Neoral Warnings)
Cyclosporine encephalopathy usually reverses after stopping; some improve with dose reduction (Neoral Warnings)
Cyclosporine: rare optic disc edema/papilledema from intracranial hypertension (Neoral Warnings)
Strong CYP3A inhibitors (voriconazole, posaconazole, clarithromycin, ritonavir): rapid, sharp tacrolimus rise despite dose reduction — neurotoxicity risk (Prograf §5.11, Table 15)
Enzyme-inducing ASMs lower both drugs' levels — see asm-interactions
sources: Prograf (tacrolimus) capsules, injection, granules US prescribing information. Astellas; revised 8/2023 (user-supplied label)
Neoral (cyclosporine) capsules and oral solution (modified) US prescribing information. Novartis; revised 8/2026 (user-supplied label)
